description: Based on the wildly popular video game Centipede. It chronicles the adventures of the elf Oliver, and his friends Centipede, Spider, Flea and Scorpion.
Oedi's origin is recapped as Dreadstar and his crew steal a massive Instrumentality treasure satellite.
Dreadstar survives Z's trap and battles him to the death. Gregzor is also killed in the story. The Instrumentality conquers Jewelworld and wins the War.
The Instrumentality begins its Holy Cleansing, the High Lord Papal recalls his childhood in this origin story. Infra Red and Ultra Violet are also introduced.
Skeevo to the rescue!?
As Vanth Dreadstar prepares to take control of the Monarchy army, he's forced to turn his attention to a threat that hits close to home, as there appears to be a traitor within his crew of allies.
"Dreadstar and Company decide to take the fight back into the enemy's camp... and the enemy is ready for them." (per solicitation)
Syzygy brings out the latent telepathic abilities that Willow was suppressing due to a traumatic experience with her father when she was a child.
"It's a fight to the finish... and we do mean the finish, for someone who's been with us for some time." (per solicitation)
"When the going gets tough, the tough take chances... maybe chances that aren't worth the risk." (per solicitation)
Dreadstar, Skeevo, Willow, and Syzygy spread out in an effort to hide from the troops that pursue them.
"The enemy continues to close in on our steadily shrinking band." (per solicitation)
"Willow is alone against Monalo, in a tale that promises to be a searing VIOLATION." (per solicitation)
"Legal precedence goes out the window, and there's just no such thing as innocent until proven guilty as our intrepid band of rebels prepares to go before a most insidious TRIAL!" (per solicitation)

Oedi saves Dreadstar and his colleagues while destroying the Instrumentality fleet with the bomb intended for Vanth.

Last Epic issue. Dreadstar moves to First Comics.
At last...the traitor revealed!
With the traitor within now taken care of, Dreadstar and his teammates begin their final assault on the Instrumentality but the Lord High Papal is waiting in "Freedom Break."
It's an all-out battle as Oedi versus Mass and Willow battles Monalo on the uninhabited world of Terigan in "Mindwar."
The Lord High Papal destroys 15,000,000 people in his city of Chichano in an effort to get Dreadstar and Syzygy, who are acting as bait while the rest of the crew steal a teleportation device.

issue_title: Victory And The High Price Of Victory

description: Dreadstar lives through much of his life in a dream sequence. His sword manifests itself as a female humanoid in love with Vanth, who awakens from a long sleep at the end of the issue.
"On his first special task force assignment, Vanth tracks down a trio of sorcerer priests. But can Dreadstar withstand the psychic onslaught of... Willow?" (per solicitation)
"Dreadstar winds up running for his life from the pyrotechnic assault of Malchek!" (per solicitation)
Vanth and Syzygy Darklock battle the Twelve Gods of the Instrumentality one last time.
Dreadstar and his gang deliver teleportation devices to the Monarchy to maintain a balance of power. They prevent an assassination attempt on King Gregzor in the process.

Dreadstar and company try to fight boredom as they travel between galaxies.  Just when they think their is nothing out there, the ship almost falls to pieces until they find an unexpected package left on their doorstep.

One infant. One betrayal. Twelve turtles. One Banana Peel. By Peter David, Angel Medina and Sam Grainger . Plus, the first installment of Pawns, an original science fiction novel by Jim Starlin and Daina Graziunas , with illustrations by Starlin.

Dreadstar and Company "Shop 'til they Drop" on a planetwide flea market, but a six-armed juggernaut named Izak has other plans. By Peter David, Angel Medina and Sam Grainger. Plus Chuck Shepard blasts off in the second chapter of Pawns by Jim Starlin and Daina Graziunas.

Vanth and the crew encounter a derelict spacecraft. It's big, heavily armed and looks like a perfect replacement for the Skeevo. Well, that's what it looks like... Plus, the third chapter of Pawns , "Maneuvering."
Called by a distress beacon, the crew of the good ship "Skeevo" investigates a forgotten castle on an isolated planet. But nothing inside is exactly what it seems.

issue_title: My Galaxy and Welcome To It
description: There's only one story on that desolate rock of a planet, and Lord Palafox is going to tell it to Vanth and Company.
Skeevo, Syzygy, and Oedi take out advertising with the Commune, an independent high-tech neutral party in the war. They meet and battle Tuetun, as the Instrumentality tries to bushwhack them.
Palafox shows his true colors. By Peter David, Chuck Wojtkiewicz, and Eric Vincent. Plus Pawns by Jim Starlin and Daina Graziunas.
Vanth Dreadstar begins to question the idea of restoring Lord Palafox to power- and the answer is treachery and betrayal.
Dreadstar and Company are trapped by Palafox's troops, and Palafox makes Willow an offer.
Dreadstar introduces Maxilon to the people. Max is a robot, designed to be a figurehead for the rebel movement. Plan M is introduced.
Vanth with help from Willow in Claudia's body battle Lord Papal, who's loses a hand in the fight.
Skeevo recaps the Dreadstar story with a definite egotistic twist. Oedi and Cookie are married.
Willow saves Dreadstar from a trap set by Mezlo. Z kills King Gregzor. Aknaton's grave is found to be empty.
Z betrays the Monarchy and schemes to get Dreadstar alone for a battle. Vanth recounts much of his past and expresses his fears that Z is really Aknaton.
Z - 7458 is seen to be a Zygotean survivor of Dreadstar's purge of the Milky Way galaxy. Z has turned Gregzor into a cyborg. He captures Dreadstar and leaves him to die.

The very sight of this girl sends him flying straight to cloud nine, but won't another year in Korea send him crashing back down?

description:
These deluxe reprint collections of 007's daily newspaper strip capture the true spirit of Ian Fleming's exhiliarating work, while exclusive features chart Bond's genesis and legacy!

Back Blurb

Titan Books are proud to present the return of the world's greatest secret agent in these library collections of classic newspaper strip adventures first serialised in the Daily Express! Ian Fleming's James Bond is back!

Brainwashed, Bond becomes a lethal weapon aimed at his boss, M, who has problems of his own: a killer whose artistry is matched only by his sadism, using pistols of gold to assassinate British agents. When Bond's mission to kill M fails, he has only one shot at redemption, a suicide mission against the deadliest assassin of them all: Francisco Scaramanga -- The Man With the Golden Gun.

This collection also includes The Living Daylights, which finds a melancholy Bond facing another sharpshooter -- a KGB sniper. Set across the jagged scar of the Berlin Wall, Bond's finger is on the trigger... and into his sights walks a beautiful blonde musician!
